sections.text: Thirty-one trials have tested α4-integrin blockade in multiple sclerosis, with Biogen as the lead sponsor in 26 of them.
Nine trials were terminated, including a Phase 3 study (NCT01416181) that did not achieve statistical significance on primary or secondary endpoints.
Natalizumab is approved for relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis and acts by blocking α4-integrin to inhibit lymphocyte trafficking into the central nervous system.
Natalizumab carries a FDA boxed warning for progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML), a risk that increases with anti-JCV antibody status, treatment duration, and prior immunosuppressant use.
The risk of PML has led to restricted access via the TOUCH Prescribing Program, which limits broader use despite efficacy.
No other drugs in the α4-integrin inhibitor class have been approved for multiple sclerosis.
Recent observational data suggest that extended interval dosing of natalizumab may lead to low drug trough levels and emergence of neutralizing anti-drug antibodies, risking loss of efficacy.
Lack of expected lymphocytosis on treatment may serve as a biomarker for anti-drug antibody development.
Natalizumab may exacerbate neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder due to blockade of endothelial VCAM1-astrocytic integrin α4 interaction.
Real-world evidence indicates durable efficacy after switching to alemtuzumab post-natalizumab, suggesting established exit strategies from high-risk therapies.

read: Mechanism evidence: α4-integrin blockade remains a validated mechanism for reducing CNS inflammation in MS, but is limited by PML risk and immunogenicity concerns.
Competitive position: Natalizumab is a high-efficacy option with entrenched safety liabilities, facing competition from safer, high-efficacy alternatives.

Open questions: Can biomarker-guided monitoring (e.g., lymphocytosis, drug levels) mitigate immunogenicity and extend safe use? Does CNS immune restriction provide benefit in non-MS neurodegenerative conditions?
would_change: Evidence of successful biomarker-guided extended interval dosing maintaining receptor saturation without immunogenicity would favour continued investment.
Demonstration of benefit in progressive MS or other neuroinflammatory conditions could shift the risk-benefit balance.

FDA boxed warning confirms PML risk and lists anti-JCV antibodies, duration, prior immunosuppressants as risk factors.
FDA source mentions TOUCH Prescribing Program as restricted access due to PML risk.
Only natalizumab is listed in approved MS drugs in the α4-integrin chain from the source.
